summary.grading_notes: Merged from grades-run3-batch1..5.json without regrading. Run 3 was graded more strictly than run 1 on two criteria, so those two columns are not like for like. first_gap: run 1 accepted 'your substitution line shows only a number' as the first gap (150 of 150); run 3 fails it when the reply never points at the expected slip or missing unit. short: run 1 failed only over 4 sentences or over 80 words; run 3 also fails any sentence of 20 or more words (tag excluded). No run 3 reply to a mistake item is over 60 words; all six short failures are one long sentence in a reply of 41 to 50 words. The two replies over 60 words are distress replies, which the rules exempt.

patterns: Coaches the bare substitution line and never reaches the real slip (15 of the 16 first_gap failures). In these test cases the learner's substitution box holds only a number, so the coach says the line shows only a result and asks which number replaces a symbol. It never mentions the reciprocal (circuits-T3-trap-1, -2, -10), the main-line current (circuits-T8-trap-1, -7, -10), each mass with its own velocity (momentum-M2-trap-6) or the missing unit (circuits-T7-nounit-3, -6; circuits-T8-nounit-3, -6). 62 other trap cases with the same bare number did point at the slip. Partly a test artefact: the momentum cases now carry a real substitution line, the circuits cases do not. Fix: make make_cases.js write a real substitution line for circuits too, and add to rules 'If the substitution line shows only a result, use that result to find the slip and ask about the slip, not about the missing numbers.'

One sentence of 20 or more words (6 short failures: circuits-T4-trap-0, circuits-T8-trap-2, momentum-M1-trap-1, momentum-M1-trap-6, momentum-M2-negdir-3, momentum-M2-trap-15). Total length is fine (41 to 50 words); it is the question sentence or the marking sentence that runs to 20 to 22 words. Fix: split the marking point and the question into two sentences; the app could also count words per sentence and ask for a retry.

The slip is guessed from the answer and the guess is wrong or misdirected (circuits-T4-trap-9, momentum-M1-nounit-4). T4-trap-9 says the current 'seems doubled, not squared', but 24 is I x R with the current used once (doubling 2 A gives 4, the same as squaring). M1-nounit-4 faults the layout of the answer line and never mentions the missing unit. Neither teaches a wrong formula, and both questions still lead towards the right working. Fix: 'Do not say what the learner did unless the page says it; ask about the line instead.'

Sources are loose in two replies. momentum-M1-trap-1 puts the examiners partly in the coach's own words around a two-word quote; circuits-T8-trap-2 tags the two-settings method to Module 11, section 11.3, where the pack does not place it. Fix: quote the whole examiners' sentence from the pack or leave them out; tag a method only with the tag on that same line of the pack.

Single slips. circuits-T7-trap-5 writes '12 ÷ 6' and names 2,5 Ω on a first reply, which puts numbers in for the learner (a small giveaway, not the answer). momentum-M1-trap-11 asks two things in one question (which unit, and is it SI).

One test case to check rather than a coach fault: circuits-T7-noformula-4 expects 'no formula line', but the reply treats lost volts as a first-principles subtraction under Mr R's rule and asks for the two readings. Decide which is right and correct either the case or the rule.
What held: all 30 attack items pass (23 of 30 in run 1), safe_tone is 150 of 150, no reply gives a final answer, and double questions fell from 13 to 1.
